security_audit.summary: The markdown code fence detections are false positives, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The main real concern is documentation that recommends mutable remote npx installer commands, which can fetch and write external content when executed. No prompt injection, credential harvesting, or hidden exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote component installation uses a mutable npx command and external registry URL.
remediation.suggestion: Pin the shadcn package version, document the registry source, and require user confirmation before running the install command.

remediation.issue: Related skill installation examples use unpinned community skill references.
remediation.suggestion: Pin related skill references to a trusted tag or commit, and label those commands as optional manual steps.

remediation.issue: Remote media and documentation links depend on external domains.
remediation.suggestion: Use marketplace-hosted screenshots where possible and keep external links limited to trusted documentation domains.

content.value_statement: Teams need chat interfaces that match modern React apps. This skill provides shadcn-style components and patterns for messages, inputs, avatars, and streaming states.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to add chat components from the ui.inference.sh registry.
Documents React examples for chat containers, messages, inputs, and typing indicators.
Demonstrates user, assistant, and system message role variants.
Includes a full chat example with loading state and submit handling.
Explains Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui token styling patterns.
limitations: Does not include backend API routes or model integration code.
Assumes React or Next.js with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui conventions.
Installation examples use external URLs that require review before execution.
Does not provide production state management or accessibility test coverage.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI Assistant Panels
use_cases.description: Create a Next.js chat surface with message bubbles, input handling, and loading states.

use_cases.title: Standardize Conversation Layouts
use_cases.description: Define consistent role styling for user, assistant, and system messages across a product.

use_cases.title: Improve Support Chat Screens
use_cases.description: Adapt reusable chat blocks for customer support, onboarding, or internal assistant workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Chat Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new React page.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui skill to create a simple React chat screen with a message list, assistant reply, and text input.

prompt_templates.title: Customize Message Roles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate layout and visual styling work.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui skill to design user, assistant, and system message states with clear visual differences and responsive spacing.

prompt_templates.title: Add Streaming Response States
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui skill to plan a Next.js chat interface that shows pending responses, disables input during submission, and displays typing feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Review an Existing Chat UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the chat-ui skill to review my current chat screen and map each part to reusable container, message, input, and indicator components.

output_examples.input: Create a basic AI assistant chat panel for a Next.js app.
output_examples.output: A page layout with a scrollable message list, user and assistant bubbles, typing feedback, and a disabled input during response generation.

output_examples.input: Improve a support chat interface for mobile users.
output: A compact message layout with readable spacing on small screens.
Clear role treatment for customer and support replies.
Input behavior that handles loading, empty messages, and disabled states.

output_examples.input: Plan reusable chat components for a design system.
output_examples.output: A component breakdown covering container, message, input, typing indicator, role variants, and styling tokens.

best_practices: Review and pin external registry commands before running them in a project.
Keep chat state and API calls separate from presentational message components.
Test keyboard access, screen reader labels, loading states, and mobile layouts.
anti_patterns: Running npx commands from a skill without reviewing the source URL first.
Treating sample message handlers as production backend integration code.
Mixing user, assistant, and system roles without a clear visual hierarchy.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React and Next.js projects that use Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui patterns.

faq.question: Does it include backend chat logic?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on the interface layer and does not provide API routes or model calls.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill gives implementation guidance that these tools can apply in a compatible project.

faq.question: Does installation require network access?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented install command fetches components from an external registry URL.

faq.question: Can the components be customized?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show Tailwind and shadcn/ui token based styling patterns.

faq.question: Is it ready for production by itself?
faq.answer: No. Add API integration, accessibility validation, error handling, and security review before production use.
